not_found: Measured radiative lifetimes of Sc I levels: the LIF measurements are Marsden, Den Hartog, Lawler, Dakin, Roberts, JOSA B 5, 606 (1988) (used by Lawler & Dakin 1989 and Lawler et al. 2019). Neither JOSA B paper could be opened (Optica paywall) and no open source tabulating the lifetimes was found (Pehlivan et al. 2015 arXiv:1509.06341 text has no lifetime table; Liu et al. JQSRT 2019 paywalled). Only lifetimes derived as 1/A for single-branch drawn levels are given, flagged "derived".
Lawler & Dakin, JOSA B 6, 1457 (1989) transition probabilities: not opened; superseded by Lawler et al. 2019 which is used here.
Branching fractions of Sc I (Lawler et al. 2019 Table 2): only a 6-row stub is printed in the paper (machine-readable table behind the IOP bot wall); not included.
Drawn UV transitions from 3d4s5p / 3d25p / upper 3d24p levels above ~37100 cm^-1: no measured transition probability newer than NIST found (Lawler et al. 2019 does not cover them).
Precise (laser / frequency-comb) absolute transition frequencies of Sc I: none found.
Isotope shifts: 45Sc is the only stable isotope; isotope shifts of radioactive Sc isotopes were not searched.
Landé g factors beyond the NIST ASD values (the NIST levels file already carries g for most drawn levels): none found.
Hyperfine constants of the drawn levels 3d4s5p, 3d25p and several upper 3d24p levels: see Hala & Nave 2022 rows included where matched; levels absent from their Tables 2-3 have no value here.
notes: Hyperfine A, B are for 45Sc (I = 7/2), sign convention of the sources (W_F = A K/2 + B[...]). All Hala & Nave values are printed in mK; MHz values here are unit conversions (flagged "derived" in the note) and the original mK numbers are kept in A_mK/B_mK. For the ground term and a4F the precise ABMR / laser-rf values (Childs 1971; Ertmer & Hofer 1976; Zeiske et al. 1976) are second-hand, read in Hala & Nave 2022 Table 2. Level energies in Lawler et al. 2019 and Hala & Nave 2022 are older values (e.g. 11519.99 vs NIST 11519.9611); levels were matched to the NIST file by energy (<0.25 cm^-1) and J. Transition probabilities A_s are Lawler et al. 2019 (uncertainties 1 sigma as printed); they rest on the Marsden et al. 1988 LIF lifetimes (about +-5%). The two unresolved y2P° lines at 4054.54 and 4082.39 A (blend of the 24656.712 and 24656.866 cm^-1 levels) are omitted. rme_J_ea0 values are derived from A_s, not printed in any source.
